Task 2: Top 15 Global Content Markets

Country-wise catalog distribution and Movies vs. TV Show split

Task 2 Market Insight: The Top 3 markets (USA: 3,240, India: 1,057, UK: 638) supply 56.1% of the catalog. East Asian hubs (South Korea: 77.1% TV, Taiwan: 82.6% TV, Japan: 66.4% TV) lead in series share, whereas India (92.3% Movies) is heavily skewed toward licensed films.

Task 1: Runtime & Season Depth Distribution

Movie duration tiers (minutes) and TV Show season renewal funnel

Task 1 Portfolio Insight: 48.9% of Movies fall in the 91–120 min feature window (mean 99.6 min). Among TV Shows, 67.2% (1,791 series) have only 1 season, highlighting an opportunity to boost multi-season renewals.

Task 3: Audience Rating & Segment Distribution

Content volume across MPAA / TV Parental Guidelines ratings

Task 3 Audience Insight: Mature 18+ (TV-MA, R, NC-17 = 45.6%) and Teens 13–17 (TV-14, PG-13 = 30.1%) account for 75.7% of all titles. Kids (Age 7+) is the only segment where TV Shows (57.5%) outnumber Movies (42.5%).

Task 4: Annual Catalog Addition Velocity (2012–2021)

Historical platform expansion by year added to Netflix

Task 4 Trend Insight: Additions surged 4.7x from 2016 (426) to peak in 2019 (2,016 titles) before moderating in 2020 (1,879) and 2021 (1,498) due to COVID-19 production halts—while TV Show additions hit a record 595 series in 2020.

Task 6: Executive Business Insights & Strategic Action Plan

Consolidated strategic roadmap across Content Planning, Regional Expansion, Audience Targeting, and Data Governance

Strategic Pillar Diagnostic Finding (Dataset Grounded) Recommended Executive Action Target KPI Impact
1. Series Renewal & Retention (Task 1) 67.2% of TV Shows (1,791 / 2,664) have only 1 season; only 17.0% reach 3+ seasons. Shift 15% of mid-tier standalone movie licensing budget into multi-season returning TV franchises. Lift 2+ season TV share from 32.8% to 45.0%
2. Emerging Market Series Mix (Task 2) India (92.3% Movies), Nigeria (91.4% Movies), and Egypt (88.6% Movies) lack local series depth vs. South Korea (77.1% TV). Expand local-language scripted series and reality slates in India, LATAM, and MEA to drive weekly habit formation. Increase India & MEA TV Show share to 25%+
3. Household Co-Viewing Slate (Task 3) 75.7% of catalog targets Mature (45.6%) and Teen (30.1%) cohorts; Kids & Family represent 23.4%. Scale animated Kids (7+) and Family (TV-PG/PG) series where episodic repeat viewing is highest (57.5% TV share). Reduce multi-person household churn
4. Release Calendar Smoothing (Task 4) Additions peak in July (827) and December (812) but drop 32% in February (562) and 24% in May (632). Stagger unscripted, docuseries, and international originals into Q1 (Feb) and Q2 (May) release troughs. Cut monthly addition variance by 40%
5. High-Travelability Genres (Task 5) International content (46.7%), Crime TV (469), Docuseries (394), and Anime (245) show strong global efficiency. Prioritize co-productions in True Crime, Docuseries, and Anime that travel across regions with low dubbing friction. Maximize cross-border viewing hours per dollar
6. Metadata Quality Governance (Task 6) 2,588 titles (29.4%) have Not Given director; 402 unattributed rows default to Pakistan. Implement automated ETL schema validation and mandatory showrunner/country attribution at ingestion. 99%+ metadata completeness across catalog
